name: Betaine
short: Two meta-analyses found betaine raised total cholesterol; one also found higher LDL, with liver enzymes and blood pressure unchanged. Its subgroup analysis suggested no lipid effect below 4 g/day.
text: In a meta-analysis of six randomised placebo-controlled trials in adults taking at least 4 g/day of betaine for 6 to 24 weeks, total cholesterol rose by 0.34 mmol/L compared with placebo, with no significant effect on LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol or triglycerides; the authors noted this might be important for cardiovascular health. A second systematic review and meta-analysis found increases in both total and LDL cholesterol with betaine but no effect on triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, fasting glucose, C-reactive protein, liver enzymes or blood pressure, and its subgroup analysis suggested the lipid-raising effect was seen at 4 g/day or more and not at lower doses. An earlier review concluded that it was unclear whether the homocysteine-lowering effect of betaine outweighs its possible adverse effect on serum lipids. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
